title: baseline
description: The appliance's runtime baseline: the policy layers and the model catalog, stored in Postgres (the `settings` row `baseline`) and edited in the administration page or with `neuman-admin baseline set` (D68). Merging with the runtime overlay is logic and lives in the decision core (docs/decisions.md D2): composition order is defaults -> roles -> overlay, lists union, set scalars win, null inherits from the layer below. The catalog half is `providers` and `models`; an entry added from a preset records it in `preset`, and the server keeps that entry's facts equal to the preset's (D76).

packages.description: The tool packages this appliance has enabled, by id (D101). A tool a package holds is present only while its package is listed here; a tool no package holds is built in. Enabling a package grants its tools to nobody  14 a role's `tools` does that. A name the release does not ship is inert, as a role granting an undeclared model is, so a baseline restored onto a release without the package loads and enables nothing for it.

providers.description: Provider name -> where it is and how to authenticate. Separate from `models` because the credential is per provider rather than per model: five models at one provider name it once, where a key path repeated five times is five places to drift.

models.description: Catalog name -> what the provider is actually sent. The key is the name a user selects and that `fragment.models` grants; `provider_model` is what goes on the wire.

fragment.description: One policy layer. Every field is optional; null means inherit. A baseline fragment lists what it grants: the subtractive {extra,only,remove} form is valid only in the runtime overlay, which this schema does not describe, so a reader of the declared configuration sees the whole grant by reading forward.

machines.description: The machines this layer may dispatch to, by label. An empty or absent list is not a refusal: enrolment is the grant, so naming machines *narrows* to the ones a role should use and never widens past a machine the account's own client logged in from. A non-empty list is a ceiling checked at the gate like any other reach.

models.description: Model catalog names the layer grants; matched against the `models` keys declared in this same baseline. Granting a name that is not declared is inert rather than an error, the same way policy for an unresolvable account is.

auto_accept.description: Approval mode. 'never' asks for every call, 'safe' asks for mutating or critical ones, 'yolo' still asks before a critical action (D23). A user may change this for themselves within `auto_accept_max`, so a value here is a starting point rather than a fixed setting.

auto_accept_max.description: The most permissive approval mode this layer allows the account to choose. Declared policy, not runtime tuning: `auto_accept` is what is in force and a user may move it, and this is the operator's bound on that movement — a role capped at 'safe' can stop approving every read and still cannot authorise its own destructive work. Null inherits; the composed default is 'yolo', which bounds nothing, because the mode actually in force defaults to 'safe' and tightening that is what a limit is for.

max_iterations.description: Model/tool steps one turn may take before the harness stops.

tokens_daily.description: Per-account daily token budget enforced by the core's own accounting (D20); null inherits, and no layer setting it means unlimited.

provider.description: One OpenAI-compatible endpoint and its credential. Neuman hosts no models (D20), so a hosted provider and a model on this machine's GPU differ only in these two fields.

url.description: The base URL. `/chat/completions` is appended to it, so this is the part before that -- `https://api.deepseek.com/v1`, not the completions path itself.

api_key_file.$comment: Not common.schema.json#/$defs/absPath: that forbids a trailing slash and parent segments, both of which this also wants, but the null case needs the union type and absPath is a bare string schema.
api_key_file.description: A *path* to a file holding the key, never the key itself (design principle 8, `docs/decisions.md`). A key entered in the administration page is written by the server to its own secrets directory, `0600` and owned by `neuman`, and this names that file (D77); a key placed by a secret manager is named the same way. The document is returned to every admin read and copied into backups, so a literal here would be published to both. Null for a provider needing no credential, which is the ordinary case for a model served on loopback.

preset.description: The provider preset this entry was added from (presets.schema.json). Absent for a provider declared by hand. A model added from a preset may only name a provider that records one of its routes.

model.description: One catalog entry. Every capability here is *stated* rather than detected: a provider's model id carries none of it, and guessing in the permissive direction surfaces as a provider error mid-turn, after the tool has run and the tokens are spent. A model on this machine's GPU names no provider: it has `local` instead, its endpoint is the appliance's runtime host, and it must come from a preset (D78).

provider.description: The `providers` key serving this model. A write naming a provider that is not declared is refused, because a dangling name is otherwise a 401 or a wrong-host request at turn time. Absent for a model run on this machine.

provider_model.description: What the provider calls this model. Distinct from the catalog name so a session keeps a stable name while an operator re-points it, and so two providers can offer one capability under different strings. This translation existed in the schema and nowhere in the code once already: the local name went on the wire and the provider answered "deepseek is not a valid model ID" (N48).

vision.description: Whether the model accepts image input, which is what allows `fs_image`. Stated, because the id does not say -- `deepseek-v4.1-flash` accepts images and `deepseek-v4-flash` does not, and a local GGUF needs a separate projector file besides. Absent means text-only, so the gate refuses with a reason the model can act on rather than failing at the provider.

context_tokens.description: The context window, in tokens: the number that decides whether a turn fits. When it was known to nobody, a local model serving 16,384 had its history managed against a 96,000-token default, so compaction never fired and the turn died at the provider instead (N86). 0 means unknown, and unknown is handled by not pretending -- the context manager keeps its own default and the client draws no capacity bar at all rather than one against a guessed denominator.

max_tokens.description: The most this model may emit in one reply. A property of the model, like the window beside it: one appliance-wide number can only ever be right for one model (N93). A ceiling rather than a fixed ask, since the harness clamps it per turn to what the window can still hold (N92). 0 defers to the server's configured default.

input_cost_per_m.description: Cost per million input tokens that missed the provider's prompt cache, shown in the model panel and used to price a turn when the provider reports no cost of its own. A user choosing between "free, on my GPU, slower" and "paid, someone else's, faster" is making an informed choice only if both facts are in front of them.

cached_input_cost_per_m.description: Cost per million input tokens that hit the provider's prompt cache. Absent means this provider does not discount them and `input_cost_per_m` prices the whole prompt. Separate because the discount is not a rounding error: DeepSeek charges $0.003 against $0.15, a factor of fifty, and an agentic turn resends the same prefix every time -- so pricing every prompt token at the miss rate overstates a warm session by up to that factor.

preset.description: The model preset this entry was added from. Its facts -- `provider_model`, `context_tokens`, `vision`, and the reasoning `control` and `levels` -- are those the preset states for the route its provider records, and a write that contradicts one is refused by name; the server re-applies them at startup, so a corrected fact reaches an appliance with the release that corrects it. Absent for a model declared by hand, which carries every claim unchecked.

local.description: Run on this machine by `neuman-runtime`, with these settings. `provider_model` is then the catalog name itself, the window the runtime is started with is `context_tokens`, and `preset` is required: the runtime starts only what a shipped preset describes, so there is no hand-declared local model.

reasoning.description:
How this model is asked to reason, and at what levels. A capability, not a tuning knob: the dialects below are mutually unintelligible, and which one a model speaks is a fact about the model that its id does not carry -- the same reason `vision` and `context_tokens` are stated rather than detected.

Absent means the model is not asked to reason at all, which is correct for a model without the capability and for one whose default is already right. The client draws no control in that case: a control that cannot work is not drawn rather than drawn and broken.

control.description:
The request shape this provider understands.

`effort` sends a flat `reasoning_effort` string. llama.cpp and the OpenAI-compatible providers take this; llama.cpp passes the value to the model's jinja template and treats `none` as off.

`budget` sends `thinking: {"type": "enabled"}` *alongside* `reasoning_effort` -- DeepSeek's shape, where the envelope turns reasoning on and the effort string sets its depth. Named for the envelope rather than a token count: Anthropic's `budget_tokens` form is removed on current models and returns a 400. The two halves are independent controls, so the level `off` sends `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` and no effort string: this dialect's `reasoning_effort` takes low/high/max and has no off value, and omitting a level is not off because the provider's own default is thinking-on.

`preserved` sends the same flat `reasoning_effort` as `effort`, and no `thinking`, and every replayed assistant turn carries its `reasoning_content`. Kimi K3.1 Pro's shape: reasoning cannot be turned off, the `thinking` parameter must not be sent, and a tool loop requires the thinking back.

`toggle` sends `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": bool}`, which is how Qwen3 exposes it for a template that understands nothing finer. The narrow case: prefer `effort` where the runtime accepts it.

`none` is the default and sends nothing.

levels.description: The levels an operator may choose from, in the order the client offers them. Declared rather than fixed because the sets genuinely differ -- llama.cpp documents minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max and a hosted provider may accept three of those. A level the provider does not know is its own error at turn time, which is why the server refuses a level this list does not contain.

default.description: The level a turn uses when the client names none. Must appear in `levels`. For `toggle`, the strings are "on" and "off".

localPolicy.description: What the machine chooses for a local runtime, beyond the window and reply length the entry already states. Typed values only: the runtime host builds its command line from these and the preset, so nothing stored here can become an arbitrary argument.

kv_cache.description: The number format of the attention cache, both K and V (`--cache-type-k`, `--cache-type-v`). Absent is `f16`, llama.cpp's own. `q8_0` holds the cache in about half the memory, so the same card affords about twice the window, and decodes a little slower once the window is full. Only matched pairs the CUDA build has flash-attention kernels for are offered: any other type drops attention to the CPU without a word (N100).
